note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM E, team 1916129: an ecological cost accounting model. A modified Cobb-Douglas
production function prices natural-resource consumption, five non-market valuations (carbon
dioxide, soil, water, dust, biodiversity) are stacked on top, pollution control and
degradation costs are added, a BP neural network supplies the long-term self-recovery term,
and the whole thing is run as a cost-benefit analysis of a house, a subway and a steel mill,
with Green GDP as the closing discussion.

A 23-page file, 17 of whose pages carry art, 25 measured regions. **All 25 are accounted**:
5 printed figures, 16 printed tables of which 15 are measured (Table 14 is the declared
deficit), 2 unnumbered halves of one appendix grid, and 3 refused vector regions. Every
figure is a single raster paste; every table is vector paths. Families: line 3, node-link 2,
table-grid 17.

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 1.3 "Symbol Description" takes **Table 1**, introduced by its heading alone.
- 2.3.1-2.3.4 take **Tables 2, 3, 4 and 5**, one constant table per valuation sub-model, all
  four behind the identical pointer sentence.
- 3.1/3.2/3.3 take **Tables 6, 7 and 8** - the control-cost grids, one per pollution type.
- 4.3 takes **Table 9**, the biodiversity service-value lookup.
- 5.2 takes **Figure 1**, the neural network diagram; 5.4 takes **Figures 2 and 3**, the two
  environmental-degradation curves; 6.2 takes **Figure 4**, the long-term cost components.
- 6.5.1 takes **Tables 10 and 11**, 6.5.2 **Tables 12 and 13**, 6.5.3 **Tables 14 and 15** -
  each case study is a cost grid followed by a benefit grid, one pointer for both.
- 7 takes **Table 16** (the sensitivity grid) and **Figure 5** (K against K/2).
- The appendix's data-sheet section takes the one unnumbered ecosystem-service grid, split
  over p22 and p23.

So the shape is: a table per priced quantity, and a figure only where a quantity varies over
time or over a network. Sections 2-4 are all tables, section 5 is all figures, section 6 is
tables again, section 7 gives one of each.

## When it goes 3-D

Never. All five figures are flat two-dimensional pastes and all seventeen grids are flat
two-column-or-more tables: no perspective, no surface mesh, no isometric projection, and no
colourbar in the file. Depth is not even faked with shading.

## What the figures do

Three line charts and two diagrams, and the split is by job:

| figure | job | how it is dressed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Figure 1 network | the model itself | eleven pollutant nodes into three media into one environment node, w_ij on every edge |
| Figures 2 and 3 | the same argument twice | twin ordinates, series coloured to match its own axis title, legend inside upper right |
| Figure 4 | the cost taxonomy | bipartite diagram, two cost nodes, nine components, two time nodes |
| Figure 5 | the closing condition | one curve with 'K' and 'K/2' written into the plot as coloured text |

Two twin-axis charts in a row with no shared scale is the paper's worst habit: Figure 2's
two series differ by three orders of magnitude, so the crossing point near year 25 is an
artefact of the axes, and the text reads it as a turning point.

## Table shapes worth reusing

Every grid in the file uses the same dress - booktabs-thin rules above the header, under it
and at the foot, no verticals, no shading, no diagonal header, full text measure (482-487 pt
of 595) even when the table has only two columns.

| table group | shape | trick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 symbols | 9x2 | italic math against prose; the table is its own section |
| 2-5 constants | 5-7 x 2 | unit inside the value cell ('198.6 $/kg'), never in the header |
| 6-9 costs | 4-8 x 2-3 | unit switches to the header ('... ($/t)'); Table 8 merges a vertical stub under 'Control Cost' / 'Storage Cost' |
| 10-15 case studies | 5-8 x 2-3 | cost grid plus benefit grid per project, both closed by a bold TOTAL with no rule above it |
| 16 sensitivity | 7x5 | transposed: projects run across the top, parameters down the side |
| appendix sheet | 8x4 + 7x4 | one grid split over two pages, header printed once only |

## Caption template

`Table N.` and `Figure N.` - a PERIOD on 21 of 21 and a colon on none, the inverse of the
usual convention - then a bare noun phrase of 6 to 13 words. No caption states a unit, names
a variable, gives a condition or draws a conclusion, and every one of them is in the passive
or nominal register (`voice` = none on all 21).

Every caption prints ABOVE its exhibit - all 5 figures, all 16 tables, no exceptions - which
is what lets the caption be typeset flush against the paragraph that introduces it and, in
Table 10's case, run onto the header line itself.

## Context connectives

- One form, used 17 times: **"The ... can be seen/shown in the following table:"** or
  **"The computed results are as follows:"** - a deictic pointer that names no number at all.
- The number is then supplied by the caption, which prints immediately under the pointer's
  last line. Every exhibit number in this file occurs exactly once in the entire text layer,
  and that once is its own caption.
- Five rows carry no pointer at all: Table 1 (heading only), Figure 1 (caption only), and the
  two appendix halves (heading only). Figure 3 is never introduced, only read.
- Four pointers print on the page BEFORE the grid (Table 2 from 2.3.1 on p5; Table 11 and
  Table 15 from the previous case study's page; Figure 5 from the last line of p18), so the
  recorded lead gap is +1 on those rows and 0 on the other thirteen.
- Read-backs are the case-study ratio paragraphs: 'the cost-ratio calculated considering the
  ecosystem services is 1.03, which means the project is not worth conducting'. They convert
  the grid into a verdict and never quote a cell.

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **Section paths weld FORWARD**: Table 2's caption heads p6 but its pointer is the last line
  of 2.3.1 on p5, and Figure 3's caption opens p14 while the paragraph that reads it belongs
  to 5.4 on p13 - both re-assigned from the prose.
- **The caption detector welds captions to their own header text**: Table 10 arrives as
  'Table 10. Cost Analysis of House Cost/$'.
- **Table 10's caption has no separate band**: it shares a line with the column header.
- **Tables 12 and 13 interleave in the text layer**: p17's region bodies for the two grids
  carry each other's numbers (2,253,581,612.85 / 81,428,571.43 print inside Table 12's bbox),
  so only the crop settles where one grid ends and the next begins.
- **The appendix grid is measured only in part**: p22's region ends inside the COD row while
  the sheet continues to the page foot, and p23 prints the rest with no header row at all.
- **The folio stops at the body**: 'Page N of 20' prints on render pages 2-21 (folio = render
  index minus one) and the two appendix pages carry 'Appendix-1' and 'Appendix-2' instead.
- **Three vector regions are page furniture**: the table-of-contents dot leaders on p2, the
  equation-rule and slur over the Cobb-Douglas variable definitions on p5, and the running
  head plus the 3.1 heading rule on p8.

## Declared deficits

**Table 14, "Table 14. Cost Analysis of Steel Mill", is printed across two pages and measured
on neither.** Its caption sits at the foot of p17 with the header row and two data rows
(Employee Compensation, Capital Input), and the grid resumes at the head of p18 with five more
rows and the TOTAL 6,769,737,111.57, without repeating the header. p17's lowest measured
region ends at y=563.6 and the caption starts at y=712; p18's highest measured region starts
at y=168 and the continuation rows run to y=146 - so the extractor left the whole table in the
gap on both pages. It is the same defect class as the one-exhibit-split-across-a-page-break
case, and it is declared here rather than counted as a row, because a row needs a measured
region and this table has none. No other deficit: every other printed exhibit in the file has
a region, and every region is accounted.
rules: The exhibit type follows the section's job, not the section's number: every priced quantity in sections 2-4 gets a table, every time-varying quantity in section 5 gets a figure, and section 6 goes back to tables for the case studies - 17 grids against 5 figures, with no section mixing the two. [place.section_kind]

Captions print ABOVE the exhibit on all 21 rows - 5 figures and 16 tables - and that is what lets the caption be welded onto the paragraph that introduces it, to the point where Table 10's caption and column header share one line. [caption.position]
The numbering is a PERIOD on 21 of 21: 'Table N.' and 'Figure N.', never the colon form, and the appendix grid gets no number at all. [caption.numbering]

Captions run 6 to 13 words and are bare noun phrases - 'Cost Analysis of House', 'Unit Service Value of Biodiversity', 'Error of the Ecological Cost Corresponding to the Different Input Error'. Not one states a unit, names a variable, gives a condition or draws a conclusion, and all 21 are nominal in voice. [caption.words]

The paper never names its own exhibits: the pointer is always deictic ('the cost and benefit can be seen in the following table:') and the number arrives only in the caption printed under it, so the recorded count of prose namings is 0 on all 22 rows. [mention.count]

Seventeen of 22 rows carry that deictic pointer and five carry none at all - Table 1, Figure 1, both appendix halves and Figure 3 - so those five are reached by heading or by caption alone. [mention.lead_pattern]

Four pointers print one page before their exhibit and the other thirteen print on the exhibit's own page: Table 2's pointer closes 2.3.1 on p5, Table 11 and Table 15 are pointed at from the previous case study's page, and Figure 5's is the last line of p18. [mention.lead_pages]

The read-back is a verdict, not a reading: after each benefit grid the prose converts the numbers into a ratio and a recommendation ('the cost-ratio ... is 1.03, which means the project is not worth conducting'), on five of 22 rows, and never quotes a cell. [mention.trail_sentence]

One dress serves all 17 grids: thin horizontals above the header, under it and at the foot, no verticals, no shading, no diagonal header - a two-column table and a five-column table are dressed identically. [table.rule_style]
Grids are typeset at the full text measure - 482 to 487 pt of a 595 pt page - even when they hold only two columns, so column width is set by the page and not by the content. [table.width]

The unit moves house halfway through the paper: Tables 1-5 put it inside the value cell ('198.6 $/kg'), and every table from 6 on puts it in the header ('Cost of Pollution Control ($/t)') with bare numbers in the body. [table.units_in_header]

Only one grid in sixteen merges cells, and the merge is the argument: Table 8's first column is a vertical stub ('Control Cost' over two rows, 'Storage Cost' over two rows) which is how the same two wastes get priced twice. [table.merged_cells]

Each case study is a PAIR of grids under one pointer - cost then benefit, three projects - and every pair is closed by a bold TOTAL printed with no rule above it and no annual column summed, so the closing row contradicts the decimal and separator discipline of the body. [table.header_rows]
Depth is never used: all five figure rows are flat two-dimensional pastes and no grid or figure carries a colourbar, a surface mesh or a perspective projection. [geometry.three_d]

A figure carries a legend only when it encodes more than one series: the two twin-axis line charts put it inside the upper right, and the network diagrams use printed edge labels and node names instead of a key. [geometry.legend]

The two figure-to-prose couplings in the paper are both wrong-way-round: Figure 4 is pointed at as 'the table below', and Figure 5's pointer ('The results can be seen by the following figure:') is the last line of the preceding page. [mention.lead_sentence]
